chunks.text: Confusion, altered mental status, slurred speech, loss of consciousness, seizures, and very high body temperature are heat-stroke warning signs. Sweating may be absent or profuse.
Call emergency medical care, stay with the person, move them to shade or a cool area, remove outer clothing, and cool rapidly with cold water, wet skin, cold wet cloths, or immersion when possible.

chunks.locator: Heat exhaustion > Symptoms and first aid
chunks.text: Headache, nausea, dizziness, weakness, thirst, heavy sweating, and reduced urine can accompany heat exhaustion. Remove the person from heat, cool them, offer liquids when appropriate, and obtain medical evaluation.
Shivering, exhaustion, confusion, fumbling hands, memory loss, slurred speech, and drowsiness are warning signs of hypothermia. Wet conditions can cause hypothermia even above freezing.

Hypothermia is a medical emergency. Move the person into warm shelter, remove wet clothing, warm the center of the body under dry layers, avoid alcohol, and do not give drinks to an unconscious person.
White or gray-yellow skin, unusually firm or waxy skin, numbness, redness, or pain after cold exposure can indicate frostbite and require medical care.
Do not rub or massage frostbitten tissue, use direct heat, or walk on affected feet unless necessary. Use warm, not hot, water only when refreezing will not occur and medical care is unavailable.
Where fires are allowed, prefer an existing fire ring. Keep the fire away from tents, structures, vehicles, shrubs, trees, and low-hanging branches, and check current restrictions before lighting.

chunks.locator: Have water and fire tools on site
chunks.text: Keep a shovel and a bucket of water at the fire so escaped embers can be controlled and the fire can be extinguished completely.

chunks.locator: Have water and fire tools on site
chunks.text: Drown all embers with water, stir the coals, and drown them again. Repeat until the fire is cold to the touch; a fire too hot to touch is too hot to leave.

chunks.locator: Bleeding Control Basic > Pressure and dressing
chunks.text: For life-threatening bleeding, activate emergency response, expose the injury when possible, apply firm direct pressure, and maintain pressure with a dressing.
A commercial tourniquet is for life-threatening extremity bleeding when direct pressure is ineffective or impractical. Apply it according to training and do not remove it in the field.
Stress reactions can narrow attention and worsen decisions. Deliberately stop, control breathing, assess immediate threats, and organize available resources before committing to a survival action.
Shelter choice depends on weather, terrain, available materials, construction time, ventilation, drainage, and hazards above or around the site.
Select signals that contrast with the surroundings, can be operated safely, and can be repeated when rescuers are most likely to detect them.
Send a distress message, activate the emergency beacon, account for everyone, put on lifejackets or immersion suits, prevent panic, and prepare the survival craft before abandoning a vessel.

Minimize time in cold water, get into a survival craft or onto a floating object, keep as much of the body out of the water as possible, do not swim aimlessly, and use a heat-escape-lessening posture or group huddle when appropriate.

chunks.locator: Wildfire hazards and Red Flag Warning
chunks.text: Warm temperatures, low humidity, wind, dry fuels, smoke movement, and official Red Flag Warnings indicate conditions in which sparks and open flames can start rapidly growing fires.
Leave immediately when officials order evacuation. Do not wait for visible flames, return through a closed area, or light a fire during critical fire conditions.
If water rises outdoors, move immediately to higher ground. Rain can occur upstream and out of sight, so a rising stream is a warning even when local skies appear clear.
Never enter floodwater in a vehicle or on foot. Reassess a stream as a group, identify escape routes, and turn back when the flow, depth, footing, or downstream hazards make a crossing uncertain.

conflicts.resolution: Do not promote one universal distance; retain the stricter local rule and describe clearance as conditions- and jurisdiction-dependent unless a displayed authority supplies the number.

conflicts.topic: cold-water survival posture versus land rewarming
conflicts.resolution: Apply posture and flotation guidance only while immersed; apply dry shelter and central warming guidance after recovery from water.

claimPromotions.text: Confusion, altered behavior, collapse, seizure, or loss of consciousness during heat exposure requires emergency activation and rapid cooling without waiting for transport.
sourceLocators: Heat stroke > Symptoms and First aid

claimPromotions.text: Confusion, slurred speech, drowsiness, loss of coordination, or unconsciousness after cold exposure requires emergency medical help and gentle handling.
sourceLocators: What to look out for; Severe hypothermia

claimPromotions.text: Continuous firm pressure limits ongoing blood loss; repeatedly lifting the first dressing can disrupt bleeding control.
Do not leave while coals, ash, or material below the surface still feels warm; add water, stir, and check again until cold.
